title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Code ships self-hosted environments (public beta Aug 6, Team/Enterprise), removes the subagent spawn cap (nested subagents now depth 3 vs 1), and gates cross-session SendMessage through the permission classifier
bullets.summary: Sessions from web/mobile/desktop/terminal/scheduled routines can now run inside the org's own network next to its internal services and security controls, while operator hierarchies get deeper and inter-agent messaging gets a safety gate.
bullets.how: The data-residency wedge: run the exact scheduled-operator fleet we build on a client's own infrastructure so a signage SMB or compliance-bound PRAGMA client keeps every byte on-prem; deeper nested subagents (depth 3, no cap) build richer operator trees and classifier-gated SendMessage makes multi-operator hand-offs safe in auto mode.

bullets.title: Claude Sonnet 5 promo pricing ($2/$10 per 1M) ends Aug 31 — standard $3/$15 takes effect Sept 1
bullets.summary: A 50% jump on the workhorse model most high-volume agent steps run on.
bullets.how: A direct Ledger line item: audit which Construct operators default to Sonnet 5 for bulk/low-stakes work and, before Sept 1, re-route those steps to a cheaper efficient tier (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, Haiku) or budget the increase; reserve Sonnet/Opus 5 for steps that actually need the reasoning.

bullets.title: Homesage.ai real-estate MCP (July 2026) wires AI assistants to 155M+ U.S. property records across 33 tools, extending the Rechat/real-estate agentic push
bullets.summary: Valuations, comps, rental projections, renovation estimates, and condition red flags become agent-callable tools for a whole records-heavy industry.
bullets.how: A live template for PRAGMA's vertical land-grab: real estate is exactly the records-heavy, locally-fragmented market where an AI-visibility + operator layer sits on top of a data MCP; watch these as substrate our owned-presence/visibility operators plug into rather than rebuild.

bullets.title: arXiv 'Multi-Agent LLM Orchestration Achieves Deterministic, High-Quality Decision Support for Incident Response' (2511.15755) — 100% actionable vs 1.7% single-agent across 348 trials, zero quality variance
bullets.summary: The paper argues the determinism of a well-structured multi-agent flow, not raw model strength, is what makes production SLA commitments possible.
bullets.how: Empirical backing for the Construct thesis: a governed operator hierarchy delivers consistency a single mega-prompt can't, which is what lets us sell an operator fleet with an SLA (uptime, actionability); pair with item 1's self-hosting to pitch a data-resident, SLA-backed operator layer.

praxis_lesson: Frontier held again (Opus 5 Jul 24 still the newest weight; GPT-5.6 and Gemini 3.6 Flash unchanged), so today's real signal is deployment control, not capability — Claude Code now runs the full session stack inside the client's network with deeper, safer operator hierarchies, and the research (2511.15755) says the determinism of that hierarchy, not model horsepower, is what makes an SLA sellable. The Construct move: package a data-resident, self-hosted, SLA-backed operator fleet as the product, keep bulk steps model-agnostic ahead of the Sept 1 Sonnet price hike, and let vertical data-MCPs (real estate and next) be the substrate our visibility and owned-presence operators sit on top of — governance, residency, and consistency are the moat while weights and tools commoditize beneath.
